headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 9 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: On the eve of the first race day, the peloton face a most demanding stage with over 5,000 metres of elevation to leave the seaside and head to summit finish at Alto de Aitana (187.4 km). The neutral start is set at 12:10 from La Vila Joiosa, the start proper at 12:26 after a 6.4 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Pogacar’s injuries
subtext: Yesterday, Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) became the first overall leader of La Vuelta to crash out of the race since Igor Anton in 2010. It was Pogacar’s first abandon since Liège-Bastogne-Liège in 2023, and his first ever in a stage race. “Tadej has been diagnosed with a concussion, displaced left clavicle fracture, a stable C7 cervical fracture, and multiple abrasions. Fortunately, no other major injuries and no neurological fallout”, said the medical director of UAE Emirates XRG, Adrian Rotunno, in a statement released by the team. This morning, Pogacar posted an Instagram story from the hospital with the Bee Gees’ song Staying Alive.

headline: A very familiar start area
subtext: Many, many riders are familiar with the area, may it be from the different races held around Valencia and Alicante, or from the training camps teams organise there in the winter season. La Nucia (km 18.1) was home to Spain’s national championships in 2021. Omar Fraile won the men’s elite title ahead of Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH). Mavi Garcia won the women’s title. And Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) was crowned ahead of Marcel Camprubi (Pinarello Q36.5) in the men’s U23 race. Coll de Rates is an emblematic ascent of the area, where dozens of professionals and amateurs rate their climbing abilities almost on a daily basis. It is also a classic on the roads of the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana, and has featured several times in La Vuelta, most recently in 2016 en route to Alto de Aitana. The race skirts around Benidorm, a classic venue of La Vuelta, who notably hosted the Gran Salida on three occasions (1964, 1987, 2011). Benidorm also hosted the road world championships in 1992. Since 2023, Benidorm is home to a cyclo-cross world cup round. Wout van Aert won the men’s elite race in 2024 and Thibau Nys (Lidl-Trek) succeeded him 2025. Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) has also participated in the event several times as a junior and U23 rider. Benidorm is also the hometown of Hector Alvarez, among Spain’s biggest talents. Currently racing with Lidl-Trek Future Racing, he is set to join their WorldTeam as of 2027.

headline: Pickering: "Pretty much all the peloton knows the course"
subtext: "The course never makes the race, it’s always the riders and I think everyone is pretty up for it today", Finlay Pickering (Jayco AlUla) announced at the start. "Pretty much all the peloton knows the course because it's not so far from places like Benidorm where we’re doing December and January training camps."

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 6.4 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Following Pogacar’s crash, Enric Mas (Movistar) leads a Grand Tour for the first time in his career. He is the first Spanish wearer of La Roja since Jesus Herrada wore it for two days in 2018. Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) is second again, a minute behind Mas. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) completes the current podium (+1’11’’) and there are six riders within 2’22’’, with Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike), Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) and Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost).

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) took 20 more points yesterday and now leads the points standings with a tally of 124. He received his 15th green jersey in La Vuelta yesterday, after he claimed 13 in 2024. His teammate Matthew Brennan is second with 67 points. Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) follows with 58 points.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Already the wearer of the polka dot jersey, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) is now the outright leader of the mountains standings with the 19 KOM points he took en route to the victory at Aramon Valdelinares. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) follows with 16 points, and Enric Mas (Movistar) is third with 14 points.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Yesterday’s stage brought no change at the top of the young riders’ standings - Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) still leads, with Jakob Omrzel in second (3’48’’) and Léo Bisiaux in third (6’07’’).

headline: Team standings
subtext: Decathlon CMA CGM still lead the team standings with a gap of 12’04’’ on UAE Emirates XRG and 20’35’’ on Visma-Lease a Bike.

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) will race with a distinctive bib today as he was named the most combative rider yesterday.

headline: Stage 9 is ON!
subtext: The riders can battle it out over more than 5,000 metres of elevation gain!

headline: First attacks
subtext: Nine riders - including Lutsenko, Cort, Johannessen - lead the way after a couple of kilometres. But attacks keep flying and the battle goes on.

headline: Lutsenko insists
subtext: The attackers have been reeled in, but Alexey Lutsnko (NSN) attacked again.

headline: 6 leaders, many counter-attackers
subtext: Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN), Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility), Alastair Mackellar (EF Education-EasyPost), Fabian Weiss (Tudor) and Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) have opened a gap of 20 seconds at km 9.

headline: 25 seconds at km 14
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) was in pursuit but he's been caught by the bunch.

headline: Thompson in pursuit
subtext: Reuben Thompson (Lotto Intermarché) is 25'' behind the six leaders, while the gap to the bunch has increased to 35''.

headline: Romele celebrates his birthday with aggressive racing
subtext: Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) turns 23 years old today. He's participating in his first Grand Tour and has already impressed with his power.

headline: 3 chasers, including Cobo
subtext: As the race passes La Nucia, Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) is chasing with Lennard Kämna (Lidl-Trek) and Reuben Thompson (Lotto Intermarché). Cobo won Spain's U23 national champion title in La Nucia in 2021.

headline: 25 kilometres of battle
subtext: Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN), Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility), Alastair Mackellar (EF Education-EasyPost), Fabian Weiss (Tudor) and Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) lead the way. Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma), Lennard Kämna (Lidl-Trek) and Reuben Thompson (Lotto Intermarché) trail by 40''. The gap to the bunch is up to 55''.

headline: Van Aert accelerates
subtext: The peloton stretches on the Belgian's wheel. The chasers are caught.

headline: The battle goes on on the first climb of the day
subtext: The six attackers have pushed their advantage up to 50 seconds as they begin the ascent of Puerto de Tarbena (7.2 km at 5.4%).

headline: 5 leaders
subtext: Fabian Weiss (Tudor) has been distanced by his breakaway companions, who are 5 kilometres from the summit of the first climb.

headline: Buitrago wants to make the break
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) is very active in pursuit of the five leaders.

headline: Counter-attacks keep flying on the ascent
subtext: With 3 kilometres remaining on the slopes of Puerto de Tarbena, the gap to the leaders is down to 30 seconds. Carlos Rodriguez (Netcompany Ineos) just accelerated. Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) also sets off.

headline: Paret-Peintre ups the ante
subtext: As a small group of riders emerge in pursuit, Valentin Paret-Peitnre takes a strong turn to try and make sure they get away from the bunch. The five leaders are 30 seconds ahead as they enter the final kilometre of ascent.

headline: Kron leads the way to the first summit
subtext: The Danish puncheur takes 5 KOM points, ahead of Alessandro Romele (3 pts) and Alexey Lutsenko (1 pt). Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) has accelerated in pursuit.

headline: Pablo Torres abandons La Vuelta 26
subtext: UAE Emirates XRG lose a second rider after Tadej Pogacar's crash yesterday.

headline: A 4-man chase group 20'' behind the 5 leaders
subtext: Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) and Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma) attacked before the summit and were then joined by Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) and Stefan Küng (Tudor). Movistar drive the bunch on the downhill.

headline: 41.4 km in the first hour
subtext: It's been a very intense start with the Puerto de Tarbena and many contenders for the breakaway. And the battle goes on!

headline: More chasers: Debruyne, Buitrago, Turner...
subtext: They are still around 20 seconds behind the five leaders after 50 kilometres of battle.

headline: New riders in the leading group
11 leaders at km 51
subtext: Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe: Fisher-Black UAE Emirates XR: Sivakov Netcompany Ineos: Svestad-Bardseng Alpecin-Premier Tech: Debruyne NSN: Lutsenko Soudal Quick-Step: Paret-Peintre Uno-X Mobility: Kron EF Education-EasyPost: Mackellar Tudor: Küng XDS Astana: Romele Kern Pharma: Berrade

headline: 15 leaders: Fisher-Black, Paret-Peintre, Sivakov...
subtext: Kevi Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike), Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) and Gijs Lemreeize (Picnic PostNL) are the last riders to make the jump to the front group.

headline: There's also a 12-man chase group
subtext: After 60 kilometres, they are one minute behind the leaders and one minute ahead of the bunch.

headline: The chasers
subtext: Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe: Vermeersch Movistar: Garcia Pierna Pinarello-Q36.5: Calzoni, Camprubi, Vader Bahrain Victorious: Valter NSN: Marti Soudal Quick-Step: Zana Uno-X Mobility: Cort Cofidis: Moniquet Burgos Burpellet BH: Diaz Picnic PostNL: Peace

headline: The second climb of the day
subtext: The 15 leaders begin the ascent of the Alto del Miserat. Among them, Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) was 2nd behind Brandon McNulty in a stage of the 2024 Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana taht finished on these slopes.

headline: The situation at the bottom of the second climb
subtext: Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Pavel Sivakov, Kevin Vermaeke (UAE Emirates XRG), Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike), Embret Svestad-Bardseng (Netcompany Ineos), Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious), Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN Cycling), Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step), Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility), Alastair Mackellar (EF Education-EasyPost), Stefan Küng (Tudor), Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana), Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) and Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma) lead the way +1'25" Gianni Vermeersch (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Raul Garcia Pierna (Movistar), Walter Calzoni, Marcel Camprubí, Milan Vader (Pinarello-Q36.5), Attila Valter (Bahrain Victorious), Pau Marti (NSN), Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Sylvain Moniquet (Cofidis), José Manuel Díaz (Burgos-Burpellet-BH), Oliver Peace (Picnic PostNL) +3'10" Peloton

headline: Sivakov and Svestad-Bardseng set the pace on the climb
subtext: Calzoni is alone, 50 seconds behind them. The rest of the chase group trail by 1'05''. Movistar pull the bunch with a gap of 3'30''.

headline: Paret-Peintre: "It's a beautiful stage"
subtext: Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) has joined the breakaway on roads that inspire him: "It's the stage with the most elevation gain, so we can say it's the queen stage. It's a beautiful stage, it suits me with a long climb at the end, just the way I like it. I like the stage. Of course, [Pogacar's withdrawal] will change the race. Pogacar is the strongest rider in the world, but he also has the strongest team in the world. We'll see if another team will be able to control the peloton like UAE has done in recent days."

headline: Buitrago takes the lead of the mountains standings
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) went first at Alto del Miserat (cat. 1). The Colombian climber has 21 KOM points now, against 19 for the polka dot jersey wearer Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility).

headline: Calzoni replaces Mackellar in the front group
subtext: While Alastair Mackellar (EF Education-EasyPost) was dropped on the climb, Walter Calzoni (Pinarello Q36.5) successfully chased the lead group. There are still 15 riders in the breakaway.

headline: 18 leaders after 80 km
subtext: Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step), Marcel Camprubi and Milan Vader (Pinarello-Q36.5) join the front group. Attila Valter (Bahrain Victorious) trails by 40 seconds. Then, Gianni Vermeersch (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Raul Garcia Pierna (Movistar), Pau Marti (NSN), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) and José Manuel Diaz (Burgos Burpellet BH) follow with a gap of 1'05''.

headline: Onto the 3rd climb of the day
subtext: The leaders begin the easiest of the six categorised climbs on today's course: Puerto de Tollos (4.1km at 5.8%).

headline: Aular sets the pace in the peloton
subtext: They begin the ascent with a gap of 4'25''.

headline: Buitrago sprints to the summit
subtext: The Colombian climber has 24 KOM points now.

headline: Valter makes it 19 leaders halfway through the stage
subtext: Around 45 seconds behind the front group,Gianni Vermeersch (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) has distanced his companions (Garcia Pierna, Marti, Cort, Diaz).

headline: Results at Puerto de Tollos (cat. 3, km 90.7)
subtext: 1. Buitrago, 3 pts 2. Calzoni, 2pts 3. Leemreize, 1 pt

headline: Vermeersch also joins the front group
subtext: There are 20 leaders with 89 kilometres to go. The gap to the peloton seems to stabilise at around 5 minutes.

headline: Mas: "We're in the lead and we have to act accordingly"
subtext: Enric Mas (Movistar) is leader on “the least expected day” (the name of a documentary dedicated to his team). “Never has a saying been more apt", the Spaniard said at the start. "After yesterday’s stage – where everyone knows what happened – today we’re in the lead and we have to act accordingly. Well, let’s just enjoy today. We have to take it one day at a time, step by step, as we said at the start. As I say, let’s enjoy the process, which is sure to be absolutely brilliant." Mas is riding at the front with his teammates around him.

headline: 24 leaders with 83 kilometres to go
subtext: Raul Garcia Pierna (Movistar), Pau Marti (NSN), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), and José Manuel Diaz (Burgos Burpellet BH) are the last entrants, making it a 24-man lead group 4'55'' ahead of the peloton.

headline: Gall: "It opens a lot of opportunities now"
subtext: The winner of the queen stage of the Tour de France 2023, Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) is among the riders set to battle at the front today. “I think yesterday, it was… the right word to describe it is a shock", the Austrian climber said at the start. "It felt really unreal to have Tadej [Pogacar] crash out of the race. I wish him all the best for his recovery. That’s cycling also, unfortunately. I think, for sure, it opens a lot of opportunities now, also for stages wins. We’ll see how it goes. I can imagine many teams all of a sudden see big opportunities now. And the race for GC now is also open. Enric [Mas] is leading by over a minute, so that’s quite a big gap. I think we just have to go day by day and there’s not so much changing for now, I would say.”

headline: Already the fourth ascent of the day
subtext: The 24 leaders begin the ascent of the Puerto de Tudons (7km at 5.3%). The gap to the peloton slightly decreased: 4'30''.

headline: The peloton move closer
subtext: They trail by 4'15'' at the bottom of the climb. Movistar still set the pace.

headline: Buitrago, a new Colombian with the polka dots?
subtext: The last Colombian rider to lead the mountains standings of La Vuelta is Nairo Quintana, in 2016. But he was leading the race and thus wearing La Roja, so Spain's Omar Fraile raced with the polka-dot jersey on his behalf. The year before, Colombia's Esteban Chaves led the GC, the points standings and the mountains standings after stage 2. His compatriot Walter Pedraza wore the polka dot jersey the next day.

headline: Buitrago conquers another summit
subtext: Results at Puerto de Tudons (cat. 2, km 121.8): 1. Buitrago, 5 pts 2. Calzoni, 3 pts 3. Leemreize, 1 pt

headline: Canal leads the peloton over the top
subtext: The gap at the summit: 4 minutes.

headline: Langellotti has abandoned
subtext: The Monaco rider was the hero of the Gran Salida. XDS Astana report he crashed on a downhill.

headline: Romele leads the way on the downhill
subtext: The Italian birthday boy has distanced his breakaway companions and will soon be at the intermediate sprint and then tackle the penultimate climb of the day.

headline: Romele goes first at the intermediate sprint
subtext: Paret-Peintre and Küng are the first chasers (48'') behind the Italian birthday boy, who begin the ascent of Puerto de Benufallim (4.8km at 5.8%). The rest of the attackers trail by a minute.

headline: More movement in the chase
subtext: Paret-Peintre and Küng are caught by Vermaerke, Cort and the rest of the chasers. Sivakov accelerates.

headline: Decathlon CMA CGM at the front of the peloton
subtext: The gap to the front of the race has increased to over 6 minutes as the peloton begin the ascent of the Puerto de Benufallim. Romele enters the final 50 kilometres with a 20'' gap to Camprubi. The rest of the chasers are right behind the Spanish national champion.

headline: Sivakov joins Camprubi
subtext: They are 20 seconds behind Romele, who is about to summit.

headline: Results at the Puerto de Benifallim (cat 2, km 139.9)
subtext: 1. Romele, 5 pts 2. Sivakov, 3 pts 3. Camprubi, 1 pt

headline: The 5th summit finish at Alto de Aitana
subtext: Alto de Aitana is a La Vuelta stage finish for the 5th time, 25 years after the first and 10 years after the last until today. In 2016, it hosted the penultimate finish, on the eve of the Madrid finale. France’s Pierre Latour got the better of Colombia’s Darwin Atapuma at the summit while another Colombian climber, Nairo Quintana, sealed his overall victory against Chris Froome. Riders of La Vuelta 26 who already climbed Aitana in 2016: 7th, Rudy Molard 15th, David de la Cruz 23rd, George Bennett 50th, Jack Haig 58th, Julien Bernard 80th, Larry Warbasse 114th, Gregor Mühlberger 116th, Koen Bouwman 127th, Michael Gogl 128th, Pello Bilbao 140th, Magnus Cort

headline: 3 leaders into the final 40 kilometres
subtext: Sivakov and Camprubi are with Romele, around 45 seconds ahead of their breakaway rivals. Decathlon CMA CGM have increased the pace in the bunch: 5'40''.

headline: The chase group explodes
subtext: There are now ten riders half a minute behind the lead trio: Vermaerke, Armirail, Vader, Svestad-Bardseng, Buitrago, Debruyne, Lutsenko, Paret-Peintre, Zana, and Kron.

headline: 16 chasers again
subtext: Garcia Pierna, Calzoni, Küng, Diaz, Leemreize and Berrade return.

headline: 30 kilometres to go
subtext: Sivakov, Camprubi and Romele still lead the way. +43'' Chase group +5'35'' Peloton

headline: Aitana is waiting for a GC battle
The final climb: Alto de Aitana!
subtext: The road rises for 22 km at 5.8%. The second half of the ascent is the steepest. Their lead on the chase group is up to 1'20''. The peloton trail by 5 minutes.

headline: 2 leaders: Sivakov and Camprubi
subtext: Romele has been distanced.

headline: The pack have begun the ascent
subtext: The gap at the bottom: 5'05''.

headline: 4 chasers have set off
subtext: Buitrago, Zana, Lutsenko and Vader have caught up to Romele a minute and a half behind the lead duo.

headline: 15 kilometres to go
subtext: Sivakov and Camprubi still collaborate. +1'05'' Zana, Paret-Peintre, Buitrago, Vader Decathlon CMA CGM have brought the gap to the peloton down to 3'45''.

headline: Labrosse is done
subtext: Scotson takes over the pace setting in the bunch. He's followed by four teammates: Riccitello, Mühlberger, Bisiaux, and Gall.
